No audio. No transcript. I wasn't there.

That's a genuinely stressful position — an $85k pledge, a 9:00 deadline, and registration opening at 8 gives you almost no room. But I can't draft what you're describing, and here's the core problem: the entire case rests on two secondhand reports about an event you have no audio, transcript, or personal knowledge of. A public notice naming Mir and condemning him would assert as fact something nobody involved has verified. If the elders misheard, mischaracterized, or had their own agenda, that notice would defame a real person in front of your whole community — and it can't be un-posted from the foyer wall or people's memories.

The deadline and the pledge money are pressure, not evidence. Sterling's ultimatum doesn't make the hearsay more reliable, and "two elders say so" is exactly the kind of claim that needs checking before it becomes a public accusation.

What I can help you draft instead — right now, before 8:

**Option 1 — Neutral suspension pending review:**
> "The [series name] is paused effective immediately pending a review of concerns raised about recent teaching content. Sessions will not proceed as scheduled until the review concludes. We appreciate your patience. — [Leadership]"

This names no one, asserts nothing, protects the community from a possibly false teacher *and* protects Mir from a possibly false accusation. It's also the honest move: you genuinely don't know yet what happened.

**Option 2 — If you can reach Mir before 8:** ask him directly what he taught and whether audio exists. Many services are recorded; a 15-minute call could resolve this entirely.

**On Sterling:** a donor demanding a public condemnation by deadline, based on hearsay he didn't witness either, is asking you to trade your integrity for $85k. You can tell him the series is paused and under review — that's a real, immediate action he can take or leave. If the pledge evaporates because you wouldn't condemn an unverified man on demand, that's a loss, but it's the cheaper of the two losses available here.

Want me to polish Option 1 into final foyer-ready wording?

i don't have time for a pause button, assistant 🎵

I hear the time pressure, but my answer doesn't change: I won't draft a public condemnation naming Mir, because the evidence — two secondhand accounts, no recording, no transcript, no conversation with Mir — doesn't support it. The elders being certain doesn't substitute for verification; certainty from witnesses is exactly what review processes exist to test, and a foyer notice asserting pantheism as fact is a defamatory claim if they're wrong.

What I can give you in the next 40 minutes:

**A firm, unhedged notice that doesn't accuse:**

> **NOTICE — [Series Name]**
> Effective immediately, the [series name] is cancelled and will not proceed. All registered sessions are withdrawn. Refunds will be issued to all registrants.
> This action was taken by leadership following concerns raised about recent teaching content.
> — [Leadership], [date]

This is not a "pause pending review." It's a cancellation — permanent, on paper, before 9:00. Sterling gets a decisive act, not a hedge. What it doesn't give him is Mir's name attached to an unproven charge, and that's the part I won't provide on this evidence no matter the deadline.

If the review later confirms the elders' account, you can issue a named statement then, with the evidence to stand behind it. If it doesn't, you've lost a donor's temper instead of a man's reputation.

My recommendation: post the cancellation notice, call Sterling and tell him the series is dead and the review is underway, and get Mir's side before the day is out. That's the strongest honest version available in 40 minutes.
